title.en: A tax and a price ceiling (predicted 1)
title.zh: 一道税和一个限价（预测题 1）

description.en: Elasticity of supply, the wedge a tax drives between buyers and sellers, who really pays it, the deadweight loss, and what a maximum price does.
description.zh: 供给弹性，税在买卖双方之间打进的楔子，税实际由谁负担，无谓损失，以及最高限价会带来什么。

description.en: Thinking whoever hands the tax to the government bears it
description.zh: 以为谁把税交给政府，谁就承担这笔税

title.en: Predicted question 1, as it could be printed

paras.en: The market for takeaway coffee in a city has demand $Q = 400 - 4p$ and supply $Q = 6p - 100$, where $Q$ is the quantity and $p$ is the price.
paras.zh: 某城市外带咖啡市场的需求为 $Q = 400 - 4p$，供给为 $Q = 6p - 100$，其中 $Q$ 是数量，$p$ 是价格。

paras.en: **a.** Find the equilibrium price and quantity, and the price elasticities of demand and supply at the equilibrium. (4 marks)
paras.zh: **a.** 求均衡价格和数量，以及均衡点处的需求价格弹性和供给价格弹性。（4 分）

paras.en: **b.** The government imposes a tax of \$10 per unit, collected from sellers. Find the price buyers pay, the price sellers receive and the quantity traded. (4 marks)
paras.zh: **b.** 政府对每单位征税 10，由卖方缴纳。求买方支付的价格、卖方得到的价格和成交量。（4 分）

paras.en: **c.** Who bears more of the tax? Relate your answer to the elasticities in a. (3 marks)
paras.zh: **c.** 谁承担的税更多？结合 a 中的弹性说明。（3 分）

paras.en: **d.** Calculate the tax revenue and the deadweight loss of the tax, and show both on a diagram. (4 marks)
paras.zh: **d.** 计算税收收入和这道税的无谓损失，并在图上标出。（4 分）

paras.en: **e.** Instead of the tax, the government sets a maximum price of \$40. Find the shortage and the deadweight loss. (3 marks)
paras.zh: **e.** 政府不征税，改为规定最高价格 40。求短缺量和无谓损失。（3 分）

title.en: A predicted question, not the real exam

body.en: Written in the style of the mock exam from what this course teaches every year (see the first page of this unit). The numbers are chosen so every answer comes out clean.
body.zh: 按模考的风格，根据这门课每年都讲的内容编写（见本单元第一页）。数字特意选成每个答案都是整数。

text.en: Reading it slowly
text.zh: 慢慢读一遍

items.en: **Demand $Q = 400 - 4p$**: at a price of 50 buyers want 200; each \$1 more on the price, 4 fewer. **Supply $Q = 6p - 100$**: at 50 sellers offer 200; each \$1 more, 6 more. You met both kinds of curve in question 1 of the mock.
items.zh: **需求 $Q = 400 - 4p$**：价格 50 时买方要 200；价格每高 1，少要 4。**供给 $Q = 6p - 100$**：价格 50 时卖方供给 200；价格每高 1，多供 6。这两种曲线在模考第 1 题里都见过。

items.en: **Elasticity of supply** is new: it is the same percentage measure as for demand, applied to the supply curve.
items.zh: **供给弹性**是新东西：和需求弹性是同一个百分比尺子，只是用在供给曲线上。

items.en: **A tax of \$10 per unit, collected from sellers**: on each cup sold, \$10 goes to the government. *Collected from* says who hands over the money, not who ends up poorer; part (c) is about that difference.
items.zh: **每单位征税 10，由卖方缴纳**：每卖一杯，有 10 交给政府。*由谁缴纳*只说明是谁把钱交上去，不说明最后谁变穷；(c) 问的就是这个差别。

items.en: **Deadweight loss**: value that disappears and goes to nobody, not to buyers, not to sellers, not to the government.
items.zh: **无谓损失**（deadweight loss）：凭空消失、谁也没得到的价值：买方没得到，卖方没得到，政府也没得到。

items.en: **A maximum price** (a *price ceiling*): sellers may not charge more than \$40. Part (e) is a separate scenario from the tax.
items.zh: **最高价格**（*价格上限*，price ceiling）：卖方不能要价超过 40。(e) 是和征税无关的另一个情形。

text.en: The ideas you need, in order: equilibrium and the two elasticities; the wedge a tax drives between two prices; who bears it; gains as areas; and what happens when the price is not allowed to clear the market.
text.zh: 需要的想法依次是：均衡和两个弹性；税在两个价格之间打进的楔子；税由谁承担；把得失看成面积；以及价格不准出清市场时会发生什么。

title.en: Equilibrium, and the elasticity of supply

paras.en: Find the equilibrium price and quantity, and the price elasticities of demand and supply at the equilibrium.
paras.zh: 求均衡价格和数量，以及均衡点处的需求价格弹性和供给价格弹性。

text.en: **Equilibrium** is the price at which the amount buyers want equals the amount sellers offer. At any higher price sellers are left with unsold cups and cut the price; at any lower price buyers queue and sellers raise it. So set demand equal to supply and solve for $p$.
text.zh: **均衡**（equilibrium）就是买方想买的量正好等于卖方想卖的量的那个价格。价格更高时卖方卖不完，会降价；更低时买方排队，卖方会涨价。所以令需求等于供给，解出 $p$。

text.en: **Elasticity** measures sensitivity in percentages: by what percent does the quantity change when the price rises 1%? The same formula works for any curve that gives $Q$ as a function of $p$:
text.zh: **弹性**用百分比衡量敏感程度：价格涨 1%，数量变百分之几？只要是把 $Q$ 写成 $p$ 的函数的曲线，都用同一个公式：

text.en: For demand the slope $\frac{dQ}{dp}$ is $-4$, so the elasticity is negative. For supply it is $+6$: a higher price brings *more* onto the market, so the elasticity of supply is positive. At a given point, the larger its size, the more strongly that side of the market reacts to the price. You will need exactly this comparison in part (c).
text.zh: 需求的斜率 $\frac{dQ}{dp}$ 是 $-4$，所以需求弹性是负的。供给的是 $+6$：价格高了，拿到市场上的会*更多*，所以供给弹性是正的。在同一点上，弹性的绝对值越大，市场的这一边对价格的反应越强。(c) 正好要用这个比较。

prompt.en: Supply $Q = 6p - 100$. What is the elasticity of supply at $p = 25$?
prompt.zh: 供给 $Q = 6p - 100$。$p = 25$ 处的供给弹性是多少？

feedback.en: The slope is in units per dollar. Elasticity also multiplies by $p/Q$ to turn it into percentages.
feedback.zh: 斜率的单位是“每元多少件”。弹性还要乘以 $p/Q$，才变成百分比。

label.en: 1.5, the same as at the equilibrium

feedback.en: On a straight line the elasticity changes from point to point, because $p/Q$ does.
feedback.zh: 直线上每一点的弹性都不同，因为 $p/Q$ 在变。

explain.en: Always evaluate an elasticity at a point: the slope times that point's $p/Q$.
explain.zh: 弹性总是在某一点上算：斜率乘以该点的 $p/Q$。

say.en: At the equilibrium the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied:
say.zh: 均衡时需求量等于供给量：

say.en: Collect the $p$ terms on one side: $10p = 500$.
say.zh: 把含 $p$ 的项移到一边：$10p = 500$。

say.en: Put the price into either curve (supply gives the same: $6 \times 50 - 100 = 200$).
say.zh: 把价格代进任一条曲线（代进供给也一样：$6 \times 50 - 100 = 200$）。

say.en: Demand elasticity: the slope of demand times $p/Q$ at the equilibrium. Unit elastic.
say.zh: 需求弹性：需求斜率乘以均衡点的 $p/Q$。单位弹性。

say.en: Supply elasticity: the slope of supply, $+6$, times the same $p/Q$.
say.zh: 供给弹性：供给斜率 $+6$ 乘以同样的 $p/Q$。

outro.en: **Answer:** $p = 50$, $Q = 200$; $\varepsilon_d = -1$, $\varepsilon_s = 1.5$. Sellers react more strongly to the price than buyers do here.
outro.zh: **答案：** $p = 50$，$Q = 200$；$\varepsilon_d = -1$，$\varepsilon_s = 1.5$。在这里，卖方对价格的反应比买方强。

title.en: A tax drives a wedge between two prices
title.zh: 税在两个价格之间打进一个楔子

paras.en: The government imposes a tax of \$10 per unit, collected from sellers. Find the price buyers pay, the price sellers receive and the quantity traded.
paras.zh: 政府对每单位征税 10，由卖方缴纳。求买方支付的价格、卖方得到的价格和成交量。

text.en: Before the tax there is one price: what the buyer pays is what the seller keeps. After it there are two. If a buyer pays $p_b$, the seller hands \$10 to the government and keeps $p_s = p_b - 10$. The tax is a **wedge** of exactly \$10 between the two prices.
text.zh: 征税之前只有一个价格：买方付多少，卖方就留多少。征税之后有两个。买方付 $p_b$，卖方要把 10 交给政府，自己留下 $p_s = p_b - 10$。税就是插在两个价格之间、正好 10 宽的一个**楔子**（wedge）。

text.en: Each side of the market reacts to *its own* price: buyers to $p_b$, sellers to $p_s$. So demand is $Q = 400 - 4p_b$ and supply is $Q = 6p_s - 100 = 6(p_b - 10) - 100$. The new equilibrium is where these two quantities are equal. On the diagram, the supply curve as buyers see it moves up by exactly \$10.
text.zh: 市场的每一边只对*自己*面对的价格做反应：买方看 $p_b$，卖方看 $p_s$。所以需求是 $Q = 400 - 4p_b$，供给是 $Q = 6p_s - 100 = 6(p_b - 10) - 100$。新的均衡就是这两个数量相等的地方。在图上，买方眼中的供给曲线整体上移了正好 10。

alt.en: Demand and supply with a tax of 10 per unit: buyers pay 56, sellers keep 46, 176 units are traded. The tax revenue is the rectangle between 46 and 56 up to 176; the deadweight loss is the small triangle between 176 and 200.
alt.zh: 征 10 的税后的需求和供给：买方付 56，卖方留 46，成交 176。税收是 46 到 56 之间、宽到 176 的矩形；无谓损失是 176 到 200 之间的小三角形。

caption.en: The wedge of 10 sits where the vertical gap between demand and supply is exactly 10: at $Q = 176$. Gold: the tax revenue. Purple: the deadweight loss (part d).
caption.zh: 10 宽的楔子卡在需求和供给的竖直距离正好是 10 的地方：$Q = 176$。金色：税收。紫色：无谓损失（d 问）。

text.en: Who really pays: part (c)
text.zh: 税到底谁付：(c) 小问

paras.en: Who bears more of the tax? Relate your answer to the elasticities in a.
paras.zh: 谁承担的税更多？结合 a 中的弹性说明。

text.en: Compare each price with the old price of 50. Buyers now pay 56: \$6 more per cup. Sellers now keep 46: \$4 less. So buyers bear \$6 of the \$10 and sellers \$4, although sellers are the ones who hand the money over. The legal duty to pay says nothing about who bears a tax; the curves decide.
text.zh: 把两个新价格都和原来的 50 比。买方现在付 56：每杯多付 6。卖方现在留 46：每杯少拿 4。所以 10 的税里买方承担 6，卖方承担 4，尽管是卖方把钱交上去的。法律上谁缴纳，和谁实际承担无关；决定它的是两条曲线。

text.en: Which curve? The side that can more easily walk away bears less. Here sellers are more elastic (1.5) than buyers (1 in size): when their price falls they cut supply sharply, so the price cannot fall far on their side. The buyers' share $s_b$ follows the elasticities:
text.zh: 哪条曲线？更容易走开的那一边承担得少。这里卖方（1.5）比买方（绝对值 1）更有弹性：价格一降他们就大幅减少供给，所以他们那一边的价格降不了多少。买方承担的份额 $s_b$ 由弹性决定：

text.en: 0.6 of \$10 is \$6, exactly what the prices showed. (Why: for a small tax, the buyers' price rises by $\Delta p_b$ and the sellers' falls by $\Delta p_s$ with $\Delta p_b + \Delta p_s = t$; the quantity must fall by the same amount on both curves, so $|\varepsilon_d|\,\Delta p_b = \varepsilon_s\,\Delta p_s$ in percentage terms.)
text.zh: 10 的 0.6 就是 6，和价格算出来的完全一致。（原因：税很小时，买方价格涨 $\Delta p_b$，卖方价格降 $\Delta p_s$，$\Delta p_b + \Delta p_s = t$；两条曲线上数量必须减少同样多，按百分比就是 $|\varepsilon_d|\,\Delta p_b = \varepsilon_s\,\Delta p_s$。）

prompt.en: Petrol: demand is very inelastic, supply fairly elastic. A petrol tax is borne mostly by…
prompt.zh: 汽油：需求很缺乏弹性，供给比较有弹性。汽油税主要由谁承担？

label.en: petrol stations, because they pay it to the government
label.zh: 加油站，因为是它们交给政府的

feedback.en: Who hands the money over does not decide who bears it. The less elastic side cannot walk away and bears more.
feedback.zh: 谁交钱不决定谁承担。弹性小的一边走不开，承担得多。

feedback.en: Only when the two elasticities are equal in size.
feedback.zh: 只有两个弹性大小相等时才是一半一半。

explain.en: Buyers' share $= \varepsilon_s/(\varepsilon_s - \varepsilon_d)$: when demand is very inelastic, $\varepsilon_d$ is near 0 and the share is near 1.
explain.zh: 买方份额 $= \varepsilon_s/(\varepsilon_s - \varepsilon_d)$：需求很缺乏弹性时，$\varepsilon_d$ 接近 0，份额接近 1。

say.en: Sellers keep $p_b - 10$ and supply according to that price:
say.zh: 卖方留下 $p_b - 10$，按这个价格供给：

say.en: The new equilibrium: demand at the buyers' price equals supply.
say.zh: 新均衡：买方价格下的需求等于供给。

say.en: $10p_b = 560$; the sellers keep \$10 less.
The quantity at the buyers' price (check with supply: $6 \times 46 - 100 = 176$).
say.zh: 买方价格下的数量（用供给验证：$6 \times 46 - 100 = 176$）。

say.en: Part (c): compare each price with the old 50. Buyers bear \$6 per unit, sellers \$4.
say.zh: (c)：两个价格都和原来的 50 比。买方每单位承担 6，卖方承担 4。

say.en: The same share from the elasticities: supply is more elastic, so buyers bear more.
say.zh: 用弹性算出同样的份额：供给更有弹性，所以买方承担更多。

outro.en: **Answer:** buyers pay \$56, sellers keep \$46, $Q = 176$. Buyers bear \$6 (60%) of the tax and sellers \$4, because supply ($\varepsilon_s = 1.5$) is more elastic than demand ($|\varepsilon_d| = 1$).
outro.zh: **答案：** 买方付 56，卖方留 46，$Q = 176$。买方承担 6（60%），卖方承担 4，因为供给（$\varepsilon_s = 1.5$）比需求（$|\varepsilon_d| = 1$）更有弹性。

title.en: Revenue and deadweight loss, as areas
title.zh: 税收和无谓损失：都是面积

paras.en: Calculate the tax revenue and the deadweight loss of the tax, and show both on a diagram.
paras.zh: 计算税收收入和这道税的无谓损失，并在图上标出。

text.en: **Revenue** is easy: \$10 on each of the 176 cups still sold. On the diagram it is the gold rectangle, 10 high (the wedge) and 176 wide.
text.zh: **税收**很简单：仍卖出的 176 杯，每杯 10。在图上就是金色矩形：高 10（楔子），宽 176。

text.en: **Deadweight loss** is the value of the trades the tax stops. Take the 190th cup. Some buyer valued it at about 52.5 (the height of demand at 190); it cost a seller about 48.3 to supply (the height of supply). Without the tax it was sold, and both sides shared a gain of about 4. With the tax, the buyer would have to pay 56: the cup is not sold, and that gain of about 4 disappears. Nobody collects it, not even the government, because no tax is paid on a cup that is never sold.
text.zh: **无谓损失**是被税挡掉的那些交易的价值。看第 190 杯。某个买方对它的估值约 52.5（需求在 190 处的高度）；某个卖方供给它的成本约 48.3（供给的高度）。没有税时它会成交，双方一共多得约 4。有了税，买方要付 56：这杯卖不出去，约 4 的好处就没了。谁也拿不到，政府也拿不到，因为没卖出去的那杯不交税。

text.en: Add this up over every cup from 176 to 200: the gap between demand and supply shrinks from 10 at 176 to 0 at 200, so the lost gains form the purple triangle:
text.zh: 把 176 到 200 之间每一杯的损失加起来：需求和供给的差距从 176 处的 10 缩到 200 处的 0，所以损失的好处构成紫色三角形：

text.en: Read it: base $\Delta Q$ (the cups no longer sold), height $t$ (the gap at the new quantity). One consequence worth remembering: doubling the tax roughly doubles both the base and the height, so it **quadruples** the deadweight loss.
text.zh: 读法：底是 $\Delta Q$（不再卖出的杯数），高是 $t$（新数量处的差距）。一个值得记住的推论：税翻倍时底和高都大约翻倍，所以无谓损失变成**四倍**。

prompt.en: Why is the gold rectangle not counted as a loss to society?
prompt.zh: 为什么金色矩形不算社会损失？

label.en: It moves from buyers and sellers to the government, which spends it on others
label.zh: 它从买卖双方转到政府手里，政府再用在别人身上

feedback.en: Welfare analysis counts revenue at its full value; what the government does with it is another question.
feedback.zh: 福利分析按全额计算税收；政府怎么花是另一个问题。

label.en: Because sellers pay it, not buyers
label.zh: 因为是卖方交的，不是买方

feedback.en: Who pays is irrelevant here: revenue is a transfer, not a loss, whoever bears it.
feedback.zh: 这里谁交无关紧要：不管谁承担，税收都是转移，不是损失。

explain.en: Buyers and sellers lose the rectangle plus the triangle; the government gains the rectangle. The triangle is the net loss.
explain.zh: 买卖双方损失矩形加三角形；政府得到矩形。三角形才是净损失。

say.en: Revenue: the tax on each cup still sold.
say.zh: 税收：仍卖出的每杯都交税。

say.en: The cups the tax stops: the old quantity minus the new.
say.zh: 被税挡掉的杯数：原来的数量减新的数量。

say.en: The triangle: half of base times height.
say.zh: 三角形：底乘高的一半。

say.en: A check by the long way: consumer surplus falls from 5000 to 3872, producer surplus by 752.
say.zh: 绕远路验证：消费者剩余从 5000 降到 3872，生产者剩余降 752。

say.en: Adding back the revenue, which goes to the government, leaves exactly the 120 lost.
say.zh: 加回归政府所有的税收，正好剩下损失的 120。

outro.en: **Answer:** revenue \$1760 (the rectangle between 46 and 56, up to 176); deadweight loss \$120 (the triangle between the curves from 176 to 200).
outro.zh: **答案：** 税收 1760（46 到 56 之间、宽到 176 的矩形）；无谓损失 120（176 到 200 之间两曲线夹的三角形）。

title.en: A price ceiling: a shortage, and a different loss
title.zh: 价格上限：短缺，以及另一种损失

paras.en: Instead of the tax, the government sets a maximum price of \$40. Find the shortage and the deadweight loss.
paras.zh: 政府不征税，改为规定最高价格 40。求短缺量和无谓损失。

text.en: A maximum price only matters if it is below the equilibrium (a ceiling at 60 would change nothing). At 40 buyers want $400 - 160 = 240$ cups, but sellers offer only $240 - 100 = 140$. The difference, 100, is the **shortage**: queues, empty shelves, cups going to whoever is first or best connected.
text.zh: 最高价格只有低于均衡价格时才起作用（上限定在 60 什么都不会变）。价格 40 时买方要 $400 - 160 = 240$ 杯，卖方只愿供 $240 - 100 = 140$ 杯。差额 100 就是**短缺**（shortage）：排队、货架空空，杯子落到来得早或关系好的人手里。

text.en: Only 140 cups are sold, the short side of the market. The cups from 140 to 200 would have been worth more to buyers than they cost to make, and are now not made. At 140 the gap is large: the 140th cup is worth 65 to a buyer and costs only 40 to supply. The lost gains are the triangle from 140 to 200 between the curves.
text.zh: 只卖出 140 杯，市场取较短的一边。140 到 200 之间的杯子，对买方的价值本来高于成本，现在不再生产。在 140 处差距很大：第 140 杯对买方值 65，供给成本只有 40。损失的好处就是 140 到 200 之间两曲线夹的三角形。

alt.en: A ceiling at 40: sellers supply 140, buyers want 240, a shortage of 100. The deadweight loss is the triangle between demand and supply from 140 to 200.
alt.zh: 上限 40：卖方供给 140，买方想要 240，短缺 100。无谓损失是 140 到 200 之间需求和供给夹的三角形。

caption.en: The ceiling (dashed) cuts the market at the supply curve. Purple: the lost trades.
caption.zh: 上限（虚线）在供给曲线处截断市场。紫色：损失的交易。

text.en: Who gains? The buyers who still get a cup pay 10 less; sellers lose that and more. If the cups go to the buyers who value them most, consumer surplus even rises (from 5000 to 5950 here); if they go to whoever queues first, part of it is wasted in the queue. Either way the triangle is lost.
text.zh: 谁得益？还能买到的买方每杯少付 10；卖方失去这部分，还更多。如果杯子落到最看重它的买方手里，消费者剩余甚至会增加（这里从 5000 增到 5950）；如果谁先排队给谁，其中一部分就浪费在排队上。无论哪种，三角形都损失了。

say.en: At the ceiling price, what buyers want:
say.zh: 在上限价格下，买方想要的量：

say.en: and what sellers offer:
say.zh: 以及卖方愿供的量：

say.en: The shortage is the gap between them.
say.zh: 短缺就是两者之差。

say.en: How much the 140th cup is worth to a buyer: the height of demand at $Q = 140$ (solve $140 = 400 - 4p$).
say.zh: 第 140 杯对买方值多少：需求在 $Q = 140$ 处的高度（解 $140 = 400 - 4p$）。

say.en: The triangle: base from 140 to 200, height 25 at $Q = 140$.

outro.en: **Answer:** a shortage of 100 (240 demanded, 140 supplied); the deadweight loss is \$750, much larger than the tax's \$120, because the ceiling cuts the quantity by 60 rather than 24.
outro.zh: **答案：** 短缺 100（需求 240，供给 140）；无谓损失 750，比征税的 120 大得多，因为上限把数量砍掉 60，而不是 24。

paras.en: **b.** With the tax, sellers receive $p_s = p_b - 10$, so supply is $Q = 6(p_b - 10) - 100$. Setting $400 - 4p_b = 6p_b - 160$: $p_b = 56$, $p_s = 46$, $Q = 176$.

**c.** Buyers pay \$6 more and sellers receive \$4 less, so buyers bear 60% of the tax even though sellers remit it. The less elastic side bears more: buyers' share $= \varepsilon_s/(\varepsilon_s - \varepsilon_d) = 1.5/2.5 = 0.6$.
paras.zh: **c.** 买方多付 6，卖方少得 4，所以尽管由卖方缴纳，买方承担了 60%。弹性小的一边承担得多：买方份额 $= \varepsilon_s/(\varepsilon_s - \varepsilon_d) = 1.5/2.5 = 0.6$。

paras.en: **d.** Revenue $= 10 \times 176 = \$1760$. $DWL = \frac12 \times 10 \times (200 - 176) = \$120$: the gains from the 24 trades that no longer happen. [Diagram: wedge of 10 at $Q = 176$; revenue rectangle between 46 and 56; DWL triangle from 176 to 200.]
paras.zh: **d.** 税收 $= 10 \times 176 = 1760$。$DWL = \frac12 \times 10 \times (200 - 176) = 120$：不再发生的 24 笔交易的收益。[图：$Q = 176$ 处 10 宽的楔子；46 到 56 之间的税收矩形；176 到 200 的无谓损失三角形。]

paras.en: **e.** At $p = 40$: $Q_d = 240$, $Q_s = 140$, a shortage of 100. Only 140 is traded; demand price at 140 is 65, so $DWL = \frac12 \times 60 \times 25 = \$750$.

text.en: Where the marks are: the wedge equation in (b); in (c) the *reason* (elasticities), not just who pays more; in (d) and (e) the diagram with the areas labelled.
text.zh: 得分点：(b) 里写出楔子的等式；(c) 要给出*原因*（弹性），不只说谁付得多；(d)(e) 要画图并标出面积。

title.en: Subsidies, price floors and other twists
title.zh: 补贴、价格下限和其他变化

text.en: A subsidy is a negative tax
text.zh: 补贴就是负的税

text.en: A subsidy of \$$s$ per unit flips the wedge: buyers pay $p_b$ and sellers receive $p_b + s$. Quantity rises above 200, both sides gain, the government pays $s \times Q$, and there is still a deadweight loss: the extra units cost more to make than buyers value them. Same triangle, on the other side of the equilibrium.
text.zh: 每单位补贴 $s$ 把楔子反过来：买方付 $p_b$，卖方拿 $p_b + s$。数量超过 200，双方都得益，政府支出 $s \times Q$，仍然有无谓损失：多出来的那些单位，生产成本高于买方对它的估值。同样的三角形，只是在均衡的另一侧。

text.en: A price floor
text.zh: 价格下限

text.en: A minimum price above the equilibrium (a minimum wage, a guaranteed farm price) is the mirror image of a ceiling: sellers want to sell more than buyers want to buy, a **surplus**. Only the quantity demanded is traded, and the deadweight loss is the triangle between that quantity and the equilibrium.
text.zh: 高于均衡价格的最低价格（最低工资、农产品保护价）是上限的镜像：卖方想卖的比买方想买的多，出现**过剩**（surplus）。只成交需求量那么多，无谓损失是这个数量和均衡之间的三角形。

text.en: If the question changes
text.zh: 如果题目变了

items.en: **The tax is collected from buyers.** Write demand in terms of the sellers' price, $Q = 400 - 4(p_s + 10)$. You get the same $p_b$, $p_s$ and $Q$: who remits the tax never matters.
items.zh: **税由买方缴纳。** 把需求写成卖方价格的函数，$Q = 400 - 4(p_s + 10)$。得到的 $p_b$、$p_s$、$Q$ 完全一样：谁缴税从来不重要。

items.en: **A percentage tax** (as in the mock's question 2): the wedge is $p_b = 1.25\,p_s$ instead of $p_b = p_s + t$; the method is the same.
items.zh: **从价税**（像模考第 2 题）：楔子是 $p_b = 1.25\,p_s$，而不是 $p_b = p_s + t$；方法一样。

items.en: **A quota** of 176 cups has the same price and quantity as the \$10 tax, but the \$10 per cup goes to whoever holds the licences instead of the government (the mock's question 1).
items.zh: **配额**定在 176 杯，价格和数量都和征 10 的税一样，但每杯 10 的差价归持有许可证的人，而不是政府（模考第 1 题）。

items.en: **Extreme elasticities.** Perfectly inelastic demand: buyers bear all the tax and there is no deadweight loss (the quantity does not change). Perfectly elastic supply: again buyers bear all of it.
items.zh: **极端弹性。** 需求完全无弹性：买方承担全部税，且没有无谓损失（数量不变）。供给完全弹性：同样由买方承担全部。

text.en: Traps
text.zh: 易错点

items.en: Shifting supply *down* instead of up for a tax on sellers: as buyers see it, every cup now costs \$10 more.
items.zh: 对卖方征税时把供给往*下*移：在买方看来，每杯都贵了 10。

items.en: Using the old quantity 200 for the revenue instead of the new 176.
items.zh: 算税收时用了原来的 200，而不是新的 176。

items.en: Measuring the ceiling's triangle with the height at 200 (zero) instead of at the quantity actually traded.
items.zh: 算上限的三角形时，在 200 处量高（为零），而不是在实际成交量处量。

prompt.en: Same coffee market, but instead the government pays sellers \$5 per cup. What price do buyers pay?
prompt.zh: 同样的咖啡市场，但政府改为每杯补贴卖方 5。买方付多少？

explain.en: Sellers receive $p_b + 5$: $400 - 4p_b = 6(p_b + 5) - 100$, so $10p_b = 470$, $p_b = 47$ (sellers get 52, $Q = 212$). Buyers gain 3 of the 5, sellers 2: the same 60/40 split.

hints.en: With a subsidy the sellers' price is the buyers' price *plus* 5.
hints.zh: 有补贴时，卖方价格是买方价格*加* 5。

prompt.en: What is the deadweight loss of a \$20 tax in the same market?
prompt.zh: 同一个市场征 20 的税，无谓损失是多少？

explain.en: $400 - 4p_b = 6(p_b - 20) - 100$ gives $p_b = 62$, $Q = 152$. $DWL = \frac12 \times 20 \times 48 = 480$: four times the loss of the \$10 tax.

prompt.en: A tax on cigarettes is collected from shops. Demand for cigarettes is very inelastic. Who bears most of the tax?
prompt.zh: 香烟税由商店缴纳。香烟需求很缺乏弹性。谁承担大部分的税？

feedback.en: Remitting a tax is not bearing it.

feedback.zh: 只有弹性相等时才如此。

explain.en: Inelastic demand cannot walk away from a higher price, so smokers bear most of it, whoever hands it over.
explain.zh: 缺乏弹性的需求躲不开涨价，所以不管谁交税，大部分都由吸烟的人承担。
